entry.name: Reach&Grasp
entry.title: Reach&Grasp: a multimodal dataset of the whole upper-limb during simple and complex movements
entry.summary: 10 subjects perform 16 right-arm tasks (hand and wrist movements, grasps, reach-grasp-manipulate) wearing a Bielefeld sensorized glove (58 piezoresistive taxels plus CyberGlove I bend sensors), with Vicon joint angles and bipolar and high-density EMG.
entry.hand: human right hand wearing the Bielefeld University sensorized glove: CyberGlove I bend sensors with a 58-taxel piezoresistive fabric lining on the palm side

sensor.note: One sample = 58 float values, one per taxel: 17 palm taxels in three groups, index and pinky 9 each, middle and ring 8 each, thumb 7. Uncalibrated (the paper says the readings cannot be related to N or Pa), although the channel files label them N. Ring-fingertip taxels rdd, rdo, rdm (hardware 9, 11, 14) malfunction.
sensor.range: uncalibrated (released values -338 to 4,906, no N or Pa conversion)

scale.text: ~2.8 h of tactile, 158 recordings (10 subjects x 16 tasks, minus 2), each with ~10 repetitions (1,603 segmented repetitions), 4 objects, one lab

entry.access: Open download without login from IIT Dataverse (DOI 10.48557/L6OWMM), file by file through the web UI, the Dataverse API or the code repository's download_dataset.sh; 2,389 files, 30.7 GB, of which the tactile CSVs are 306 MB.
caveats: Simple reach-and-grasp and single-DoF movements with 4 objects, not dexterous manipulation; right hand only.
No video released: sessions were video-recorded, but the video is only available on request.
Tactile values are uncalibrated, although the channels.tsv files and Supplementary Table 6 label them N.
Ring-fingertip taxels rdd, rdo and rdm (hardware IDs 9, 11, 14) malfunction (paper); taxel lmo reads 0 in all 158 tactile files.
Many taxels read exactly 0 for a whole recording, and 10 tactile files (non-contact tasks: wrist movements, hand opening, frontal reach) are entirely 0.
sub-03 FroRea and ReaCyl have no tactile or CyberGlove files (EMG and Vicon only).
sub-01 Trid tactile channels.tsv has 116 rows: 58 junk names (numbers from the first data row), then the 58 real names.
Each file is one continuous recording of ~10 repetitions; repetition boundaries are in code/Events_Reach&Grasp.mat in the code repository, not in the dataset.
Vicon data is released as joint angles only (no marker trajectories).
CSV files have no header; time is column 0 and channel names are in the matching channels.tsv.

tracking.system: Vicon (10 infrared cameras, Lock+ sync; 23 reflective markers in total), RHand Bodybuilder model in Vicon Nexus 2.12.1
tracking.note: 100 Hz joint angles only: MCP of each finger (Abs flexion + Proj flexion/abduction) and thumb STT and MCP; no marker trajectories released
100 Hz X/Y/Z joint angles of left and right thorax, right shoulder, elbow and wrist

tracking.system: CyberGlove I (Version 1.1) inside the Bielefeld glove, recorded over ROS
tracking.note: 100 Hz, 18 angles in degrees: thumb rotation/MCP/IP/abduction, MCP and PIP of index..pinkie, three inter-finger abductions, palm arch, wrist pitch and yaw; sensor-to-angle scaling tuned per subject

other: HD-sEMG 64 ch (OT Bioelettronica Sessantaquattro, two 32-electrode GR10MM0804 grids on forearm flexors and extensors, monopolar, 2 kHz)
bipolar EMG 10 ch (Cometa Wave Plus, arm and shoulder muscles, 2 kHz)
session video recorded but not released (on request)

unconfirmed: hours = 2.76: sum of RecordingDuration over the 158 tactile JSON sidecars (9,949.3 s), equal to the 995,088 tactile CSV rows / 100 Hz. Over all 160 recordings (EMG and Vicon) it is 10,056.9 s = 2.79 h.
frames = 995,088: total rows of the 158 released tactile CSVs (100 Hz).

episodes = 158 tactile recordings (one per subject-task); 160 recordings exist for EMG and Vicon. Events_Reach&Grasp.mat holds 1,603 start/end pairs (151 recordings with 10, 6 with 11, 3 with 9), versus the paper's '10 repetitions each'.
objects = 4 from Table 2 and Fig. 3B: glass (78 mm), bottle with a 28 mm screw cap, ping-pong ball (38 mm), tennis ball (67 mm); the table and the water are not counted.
scenes = 1: all tasks in one Vicon volume (5.1 x 4.2 x 2.5 m), subject seated at a table (Fig. 3A).
Recording durations 27.9-124.7 s (median 62.8 s) from the tactile JSON sidecars; all modalities of one subject-task share the same RecordingDuration.

CSV column i (1-58) maps to hardware taxel IDs 1-48 for i <= 48, and columns 49-58 to IDs 51, 54, 55, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63 (Supplementary Table 5 numbers IDs 1-65 with 49, 50, 52, 53, 56, 64, 65 unused; Fig. 2A uses the hardware IDs). Checked by matching the channels.tsv order to Supplementary Table 5 and by overlaying the 58 positions of Curser_Reach&Grasp.mat (reversed order, as in Figure_9.m) on glove_mapping.JPG.

All-zero taxels: in the 158 tactile files, the number of taxels that are exactly 0 for the whole file ranges 3-58 (median 43); lmo is 0 in 158/158, ldo 156, lpo 155. Entirely zero files: sub-07 WE, WS; sub-08 WE, WP, WS; sub-09 FroRea, HO, WF, WP; sub-10 WS.
Value range over all tactile files: -337.8 to 4,906.4; on average 7.1% of samples are negative. In sub-01 Cyl the malfunctioning rdd and rdo never read 0 (58-94 and 5-73).
The paper says the glove PC ran ROS Melodic on Ubuntu 20.04; the tactile and CyberGlove JSON sidecars say 'ROS Noetic'.
Paper Fig. 2 counts are 17 palm, 9 index, 8 middle, 8 ring, 9 pinky, 7 thumb; Supplementary Table 5 names give the same split (palm: 5 PalmWrist, 6 PalmThumb, 6 PalmFinger).

sample.fetch_estimate: ~48 MB: tactile CSVs 21.9 MB (all 158 tactile CSVs, 306 MB, were already downloaded during the survey to ~/data/ext/reachgrasp/tactile), CyberGlove CSVs 14.1 MB, Vicon CSVs 12.1 MB, plus channels.tsv/json sidecars (<0.1 MB). Not planned: bipolar EMG 190 MB and HD-EMG 1.11 GB for these 8 recordings.
sample.rules_applied: 16 tasks > 6, so 8 were taken, one episode each (8 total). All tasks happen in one lab and are right-hand only, so the spread is over action types and objects: whole-hand self-contact (HC), power grasp on a sphere (Sph, tennis ball) and a cylinder (Cyl, glass), precision grasp (Trid, ping-pong ball), twist (Screw, bottle cap), pour (Pour, glass with water), transport (EatFruit, tennis ball) and no-object fingertip contact (Thumb). Left out: WP, WS, WF, WE, HO and FroRea (no object; 10 of their files are entirely 0 and most others show no sustained contact) and ReaCyl/ReaSph (same grasps as Cyl/Sph after a reach, already covered by Pour/Screw/EatFruit). Within a task the file with the fewest whole-file-zero taxels and clear repetitions was chosen, spreading subjects (7 subjects; sub-04 twice). Channel check on every pick: 58 tactile columns plus time, no NaN, time step exactly 0.01 s, channels.tsv names identical to sub-01 Cyl (58 rows); CyberGlove and Vicon rows equal tactile rows (checked on sub-01 Cyl: 5,936 each). Dead taxels are a property of the glove (lmo 0 in every file; rdd/rdo/rdm malfunction per paper) and are listed per episode in the converter notes, not treated as corruption. Contact test: rest = per-taxel median of the first 1 s (before the first repetition), activation = sum over taxels of max(0, x - rest), contact = activation > max(500, mean + 10 sd of the first second); every pick has >= 7 contact runs of >= 1 s. Duration 10-60 s: four files fit whole; Screw, Pour and EatFruit (66-86 s) are cut to [0, 59-60] s at a repetition boundary from the code repo's Events_Reach&Grasp.mat (sample indices at 100 Hz). Budget: 58 taxels x <= 6,000 frames as uint8 is ~0.46 MB base64 per episode, under 2 MB; no media to re-host.

used as the 100 Hz clock (row index; identical time column in the tactile, CyberGlove and Vicon CSVs, checked)
